title: Delhi AQI Hits 389 as 18 Stations Record Severe Air Before Diwali
excerpt: The capital's air stayed 'very poor' for a fourth day on Friday, with Rohini and IIT Delhi at 474 and forecasts warning of severe air through the Diwali weekend.
body:
• Delhi's 24-hour average AQI was 389 at 8 a.m. on Friday, November 6, up from 369 on Thursday — 'very poor' for a fourth consecutive day, according to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).
  • Of 59 active monitoring stations, 18 recorded 'severe' air on Thursday; on Friday, IIT Delhi and Rohini both read 474, Punjabi Bagh 465 and RK Puram 443.
  • The Air Quality Early Warning System forecasts severe air from November 6 to 8, with severe-to-very-poor conditions for the following six days — covering Diwali on November 8.
  • Under CPCB bands, 301–400 is 'very poor' and 401–500 is 'severe'; municipal teams deployed water sprinklers around India Gate under GRAP Stage II.

Delhi's air quality remained in the 'very poor' category for the fourth consecutive day on Friday, with the 24-hour average Air Quality Index at 389 at 8 a.m., compared with 369 on Thursday, The Times of India reported, citing CPCB data. Several areas crossed into 'severe': IIT Delhi and Rohini recorded 474 each, followed by Punjabi Bagh at 465, RK Puram at 443, ITO at 422, Feroz Shah Road at 420 and India Gate at 403. Anand Vihar and Akshardham read 359, IGI Airport Terminal 3 read 385, Aya Nagar 393 and Chandni Chowk 391.

Half the city in the red on Thursday

Of the 59 active monitoring stations in the capital, 18 recorded 'severe' air quality on Thursday, with Jahangirpuri registering the highest AQI of 454 at 4 p.m., according to CPCB data reported by The Daily Jagran. Under CPCB standards, an AQI of 0–50 is 'good', 51–100 'satisfactory', 101–200 'moderate', 201–300 'poor', 301–400 'very poor' and 401–500 'severe'.

Municipal authorities deployed truck-mounted water sprinklers around India Gate under Stage II of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP), India Today reported. The Decision Support System for air-quality management estimated that crop-residue burning accounted for 15.601% of Delhi's pollution contribution on Thursday.

Forecast: worse before it gets better

According to the Air Quality Early Warning System, Delhi's air is likely to remain very poor on Friday before deteriorating to severe from November 6 to 8, and the outlook for the subsequent six days is severe to very poor. Experts cited in the reports said weakening winds could trap pollutants over the city, with a further spike anticipated in the days following the festival. The India Meteorological Department recorded a morning temperature of 17.8°C on Friday, with mainly clear skies, shallow fog forecast over the next four days and fog or mist on the mornings of November 10 and 11.

Fireworks window

The Supreme Court has permitted green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR on November 7 and 8 between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. and between 8 p.m. and 10 p.m., ahead of Diwali on November 8, with a complete ban on firecrackers returning from November 9, IANS reported earlier this week. That window falls inside the forecast severe-air period, which is why the next 72 hours — not the festival day alone — are the stretch residents and visitors are being warned about.
